tip: нравится (nravitsya) puts the liker in the dative: Ей нравится (Yey nravitsya = to her it pleases). The liked thing is the subject.
интересуюсь (interesuyus') takes the instrumental for the topic, with no preposition: историей (istoriey = in history).
улыбается (ulybayetsya) takes the dative for who you smile at: детям (detyam = at the children). Russian smiles 'to' someone.
отказывается (otkazyvayetsya) uses от plus the genitive for what is declined: от помощи (ot pomoshchi = help).
обращается (obrashchayetsya) takes к plus the dative for turning to someone: к врачу (k vrachu = to a doctor).
извиняюсь (izvinyayus') uses за plus the accusative for what you apologize for: за опоздание (za opozdaniye = for being late).
сердится (serditsya) uses на plus the accusative for who you are angry at: на брата (na brata = at her brother).
чувствую себя (chuvstvuyu sebya): the reflexive себя is required to say how you feel: чувствую себя хорошо (...khorosho = I feel good).
умываюсь (umyvayus') ends in -ся (-sya) meaning wash oneself, so no separate 'my face' is needed: Я умываюсь (Ya umyvayus').
за plus the instrumental marks a static location: за деревом (za derevom = behind a tree). Motion to behind would take the accusative.
везёт (vezyot) is impersonal 'to be lucky'; the lucky person goes in the dative: Мне везёт (Mne vezyot = I am lucky), with no 'I' subject.
дороже (dorozhe = more expensive) is the comparative; what you compare against takes the genitive with no word for 'than': того (togo = that one).
With чем (chem = than) the comparison is spelled out and needs a comma: свежее, чем вчера (svezheye, chem vchera = fresher than yesterday).
самый (samyy) plus an adjective forms the superlative 'the most': самый дорогой (samyy dorogoy = the most expensive).
бы plus a past-tense verb makes the conditional 'would': Он бы написал (On by napisal = he would write). бы can shift position in the clause.
хотел бы (khotel by) softens want into 'would like', gentler than хочет (khochet = wants). бы plus past makes a polite wish.
сейчас (seychas) means 'now', but with a future verb it means 'in a moment': сейчас вернусь (seychas vernus' = I will be right back).
